text:
incident-bot: Pager | Elevated 5xx rate detected on api-gateway (apigw-eu-west) starting ~2026-03-15T07:01:10Z. Current 5xx rate: 28% on /v1/generate, P50 latency 360ms, P95 2.8s. Auto-notify to #incidents and on-call team.
Ashwin: Acked. I'm oncall. Confirming scope — is this only eu-west region?
Maria: Looks like eu-west primarily, small correlated bump eu-central. Traffic pattern: spike at 07:01, sustained. Most errors are 502/504 with upstream connect errors in edge logs.
Julian: I see a lot of upstream timeout messages in nginx: 
```
2026/03/15 07:01:14 [error] 1234#0: *987654 connect() failed (110: Connection timed out) while connecting to upstream, client: 10.0.0.12, server: apigw, request: "POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://10.1.22.45:8080/generate"
```
Maria: Backend pool apigw-proxies-prod-1 is reporting elevated conn queues. Backend healthchecks show 30% unhealthy on pool-1.
Leah-SRE: Can anyone dump the HAProxy stats and ingress queue length? Also paste output of `ss -s` from the apigw hosts.
Ashwin: grabbing HAProxy stats from apigw-12: 
```
# echo "show stat" | socat stdio /var/run/haproxy.sock
pxname,svname,scur,stot,bin,bout
apigw-front,FRONTEND,4500,123456,234M,450M
proxy-pool-1,backend,120,3000,34M,78M
proxy-pool-2,backend,8,200,2M,4M
```
Ashwin: pool-1 has high scur and errors, pool-2 seems healthy but lower capacity.
Remy: Are we autoscaling pool-2 or can we shift some traffic?
Julian: We have a routing policy to prefer pool-1 by weight. If we scale pool-2 and adjust weights, that should reduce errors quickly.
Maria: I can scale pool-2 now. Suggest `kubectl scale deployment apigw-proxy-pool-2 --replicas=18 -n prod` and then update traffic weights.
Ashwin: Doing the scale now. Running `kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=apigw-proxy-pool-2`
ops-bot: Command accepted: scale deployment apigw-proxy-pool-2 -> 18 replicas. Pods starting (expected 6m rollout).
Ashwin: Rolling update in progress. Meanwhile enable routing fallback to pool-2 with lower weight shift:
```
# temporary weight tweak
apigw-routes set-weight --route /v1/generate --backend pool-2 --weight 40
```
Leah-SRE: Also enable short-term circuit breaker on /v1/generate to reject long tail clients, threshold 5xx > 10% for 30s -> return 503 with Retry-After. That prevents downstream cascading.
Ashwin: Applying circuit breaker rule now.
ops-bot: Circuit breaker rule added for /v1/generate: 5xx_threshold=10%, window=30s, fallback_code=503
Maria: After weight shift we see immediate drop in 502s from 28% to 12% at edge. P95 latency dropping to 1.1s.
Julian: Good. Still seeing some timeouts from origin model pools; looks like a subset of model-hosts hitting CPU saturation and accept backpressure slowly. Can we temporarily disable expensive eval-mode on some hosts?
Remy: I can disable background evals and reduce batch size on those hosts (`--max-batch 8`). On it.
Emily-CS: Quick customer impact note: CS triage — which customers are impacted? We have two enterprise tenants using eu-west routed exclusively via dedicated nodes.
Maria: Customer list: acme-corp (100% traffic eu-west), orbit-saas (partial). Acme experiencing failures for ~7 minutes since 07:01. Estimated request loss ~20k requests.
Emily-CS: Notifying acme priority channel now with initial statement: "We're investigating elevated errors in eu-west; mitigation in progress. ETA 20-30min for stabilization."
Leah-SRE: Monitoring suggests stabilization continuing. Need to keep circuit breaker for another 15m and keep scaling until pool-1 health improves. We should also check upstream firewall logs for any SYN drops.
Ashwin: Checking `ss -s` on apigw-12: 
```
Total: 12345 (estab 4500)
TCP: RTO=56, SYNs=120, orphaned=3, timewaits=1500
```
Ashwin: No obvious kernel drop. Metrics show conn_wait increasing on certain backends.
Julian: I've opened a short-term bypass route to go straight to pool-2 for acme-corp only — header-based routing override. That reduces customer impact.
Remy: Background evals disabled on problematic hosts, batch size reduced, CPU usage on those nodes dropping from 94% to 62% over 60s.
Maria: Pool-1 health now 85% healthy (was 70). 5xx rate at edge down to 6% overall.
incident-bot: Incident declared: SEV2 | api-gateway 502/504 spike in eu-west. Incident leads: Ashwin (oncall), Leah-SRE (SRE lead).
Ashwin: I'm going to keep the channel for live mitigation. If anyone sees recurrence, ping me. I'll coordinate handoff to Leah for post-incident clean-up and root cause.
Leah-SRE: I'll take 1hr to stabilize and run sweeps: review HAProxy config, connection timeouts, tune keepalive and upstream healthchecks. We'll schedule postmortem.
Emily-CS: CS update posted to affected customers and we created an internal CV/CS briefing doc. ETA for final customer message: 11:30 UTC after RCA.
Julian: Quick note: add a prom alert for backend conn_queue growth > 100 for 2m, and create a runbook step to auto-shift weights if pool health < 80%.
Remy: Will add runbook snippet and alert, pushing as PR now.
Ashwin: Thanks all. Dropping from active now — Leah will own the handoff.
Leah-SRE: Handoff acknowledged. I'll post status update in 30m.
Emily-CS: Marking support tickets with "mitigated, monitoring" and will follow up once RCA is ready. :thumbsup:
Ashwin: closing the active pager. Good job team.
incident-bot: Pager resolved for current spike. Channel remains for postmortem and follow-ups.
